title: introduce-temporal-tilt-detector-and-daypart-smoothing-dashboard
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: transient daypart and seasonal patterns were generating noisy token-cost alerts and paging on short-lived shifts. This PR implements a lightweight 'Temporal Tilt Detector' that combines a daypart-aware baseline (hour-of-day/week-of-day bucketing), an EWMA trend baseline, and a seasonal-trend decomposition stage to produce a bounded tilt_score per route/tenant. The tilt_score is emitted as a low-cardinality metric and as a span tag to enable correlated traces for root-cause. Changes include: (1) new telemetry exporter fields (tilt_score, daypart, rolling_baseline) and bounded aggregation keys; (2) trace enrichment for tilt tagging; (3) a Grafana dashboard "Daypart Tilt & Cost Smoothing" with panels for tilt, smoothed token-cost, raw vs baseline, per-tenant drift heatmap and suggested mitigation actions; (4) updated alert rules that use dampening (15m suppression window for small tilts) and hysteresis to avoid flapping; (5) incident-bot integration to defer low-severity pages automatically when tilt is transient and non-regressive; (6) unit + integration tests and a micro-benchmark to validate detector latency on median payloads. Design notes: to control cardinality we bucket daypart into 6 coarse zones and restrict tilt emission to aggregation keys {route, model_family, tenant_tier} by default with an opt-in fine-grained label. We include a sampling guard for high-cardinality tenants and aggregate sketches for rollups. See docs link: RFC https://linear.app/redwood/ENG-1987 for algorithm rationale. Checklist: [x] implement detector algorithm prototype; [x] exporter + trace tag; [x] Grafana dashboard; [x] alert rule changes; [x] tests and bench; [x] docs and quickstart example.

review_comments: Ethan Liu: Overall great direction. Concern: tilt_score might create high-cardinality if we emit with fine-grained labels. Can we ensure default emission is aggregated?
Priya Natarajan: Alert dampening makes sense. Please add a runbook stanza that lists manual override steps and how to revert the suppression window quickly in case of regression.
Liam O'Connor: Performance: detector runs in the ingest hot path. Bench shows 1.6ms median, but I'm seeing P95 at 12ms in initial runs. Need to validate under burst (10k rps).
SRE Team (comment): Prometheus scrape and storage impact needs estimates. Provide expected cardinality delta and retention guidance.
author_replies: Maya Patel: Addressed cardinality by defaulting daypart -> 6 coarse bins and emitting tilt only for aggregation keys {route, model_family, tenant_tier}. Added opt-in label 'tilt_detail=true' for customers who want per-call tilt. Sampling guard added for >1k unique tenants per minute.
Maya Patel: Added runbook section in docs with explicit steps to toggle alert dampening and suggested rollback play. Saved a sample Linear task for runbook follow-ups ENG-1999.

Maya Patel: Investigated perf: optimized hot-path by moving seasonal smoothing to async micro-batch when latency budget tight. Re-ran bench: median 0.9ms, P95 3.8ms under 10k rps synthetic load (see bench_results.md).

Maya Patel: Included a small cardinality impact table and retention recommendations in the RFC. Prometheus storage impact estimated <3% for default config; opt-in detailed mode increases cardinality and should be monitored.
